object_description: compact four-storey cube with a partly sunken auditorium
design_condition: Placed at the northeast interface between the school and neighborhood, the compact tower aligns with the surrounding orthogonal structure, preserves most trees and meadow, and creates clearly contained open spaces.

positive.statement: The setting and volumetrics appear harmonious in context.
The compact footprint allows generous outdoor spaces and preserves most of the trees.
The positioning at the interface between neighborhood and school is consistent.
The division of uses works on the upper floors.
The structure is neatly constructed in wood and wood-concrete composite construction.
The implementation of the environmental standard is carefully described and feasible.

negative.statement: The cube-shaped building appears rather dominant in the area.
The auditorium is introverted and has little external impact on the school or neighborhood.
The vertical access and the auditorium’s shape and arrangement are not convincing.
The facade appears arbitrary and does not reflect the floor-plan layering or uses.
The facade lacks the powerful architectural character of the existing complex.
The project would require substantial organizational reworking, especially for the daily structures.
The generous access zones and basement are unfavorable economically.
The winter gardens and terraces have disadvantageous cost and energy effects.
The usefulness of the upper terrace is questioned.
